vocabulary.definition: The user-facing name for one automation: a directed graph of actions wired by edges with exactly one trigger action. Stored as a HogFlow row.
The internal code and model name of a workflow (HogFlow, hog_flow, /hog_flows API). Appears only in code identifiers and routes, never in UI copy, MCP descriptions or skills.

One id-addressed node of the workflow graph. Its type comes from the closed set SUPPORTED_ACTION_TYPES (trigger, function, function_email, function_sms, function_push, delay, wait_until_condition, wait_until_time_window, conditional_branch, random_cohort_branch, exit). The editor calls it a step.
A directed link from one action to the next. A continue edge is the fall-through or timeout path; a branch edge carries an index into the source action's conditions or cohorts.

The single trigger action that starts every run. Its config.type is the trigger type (event, batch, schedule, webhook, manual, tracking_pixel, data-warehouse-table, data-warehouse-view, internal-event). The top-level trigger field is derived from it and read-only.
A trigger whose runs have no PostHog person: data-warehouse-table, data-warehouse-view and internal-event (Slack, GitHub). Person-dependent actions are rejected on these workflows.
The lifecycle state of the live workflow row: draft, active or archived. Changed by explicit lifecycle actions (enable, disable, archive).
Pending content edits held in the draft column of an active workflow. Nothing reaches people until it is published or discarded.
Promote the staged draft to the live row after strict revalidation and a publish-impact preview. Bumps version and appends a revision.
An append-only snapshot of a workflow's live content at one version. Restoring a revision copies it into the staged draft; workers never read revisions.
The integer on the live workflow that identifies which content produced a metric. Metrics are keyed <flow id>/<version> under app_source hog_flow_version.
One execution of a workflow for one person or row, persisted as an invocation (Cyclotron job) that can park on a delay or wait and wake later.
A one-off dispatch of a batch-trigger workflow to a person audience defined by person properties or cohorts. Broadcast is the product surface built on batch workflows.
A recurring cadence (rrule, timezone, variables) attached to a batch or schedule workflow; the scheduler reads the live trigger when it fires.
The audience preview for a batch dispatch. It returns the recipient count and a confirm token bound to the stored trigger filters that programmatic dispatch must present.
A goal (events and property filters within a window) counted at most once per run and credited to the version that sent the message.
A Hog template (template_id) that a function step runs, from nodejs/src/cdp/templates. Email, SMS and push steps use the fixed literals template-email, template-twilio and template-native-push.
A saved library message design referenced by template_uuid. Its body is snapshotted into the step at save; later template edits do not propagate.
A function-step or trigger input marked secret in its template schema. It is stored encrypted in encrypted_inputs and returned as {secret: true}.

components.name: Workflow API
components.responsibility: The hog_flows DRF viewset and serializers: the write chokepoint that validates action configs and graph structure, compiles bytecode, masks secrets, routes active-workflow edits to drafts and declares API scopes.

components.name: Draft and revision store
components.responsibility: The HogFlow row (live content, staged draft, version, encrypted inputs), append-only HogFlowRevision snapshots, and the management commands that rewrite stored rows.

components.name: Flow manager
components.responsibility: Loads and caches workflows for the Node workers, merges decrypted secret inputs, and reacts to reload signals from Django.

components.name: Executor
components.responsibility: Walks a run through the graph one action at a time via a handler per action type, parks and wakes delays and waits, evaluates exits and conversions, and runs test invocations.

components.name: Batch and schedule dispatcher
components.responsibility: Resolves batch audiences, gates dispatch on an active workflow and a blast-radius confirm token, and fires recurring schedules.

components.name: Editor
components.responsibility: The kea logics and scenes that load, edit, autosave, stage and publish workflows and broadcasts, and parse every action against the editor's strict step schema.

components.name: Step and trigger registry
components.responsibility: Side-effect registrations of trigger types and action categories, the Hog templates steps run, and async functions available to Hog code.

components.name: Messaging providers
components.responsibility: Sends email, SMS and push through SES, Twilio and native push, and handles sender domains, tracking codes, sending tiers and reputation.

components.name: Metrics and conversions
components.responsibility: Emits app metrics under hog_flow and hog_flow_version, watches conversion goals, and exposes Prometheus counters for silent degradations.

components.name: Agent surface
components.responsibility: The MCP tool definitions generated from the OpenAPI schema, plus the building-workflows and designing-email-templates skills that teach agents the graph contract.

components.name: Facade
components.responsibility: The product's public Python surface for other products and core; today a small api.py.

sourceNotes: 715 human comments across 211 PRs; mayteio (299), dmarchuk (140) and meikelmosby (92) dominate. Many human-account comments are agent-written replies to bot findings (Claude Code, talyn.dev); they were used as evidence of the rule the author accepted, not as independent reviewers.

About 190 'Fixed in / Thanks / LGTM' replies and one-off findings (UI copy, layout nits, SES metric math, rrule picker state, papaparse pinning) were ignored unless the same class recurred across PRs.

Of 1520 bot comments (posthog 663, greptile 377, coderabbit 152, stamphog 95, veria 92), a handful were cited where they corroborated a human rule: secret masking, base_updated_at fencing, person:read scopes, blast-radius review.

Code checks at 57ca357 found no workflows-specific semgrep or oxlint rules; most cross-language invariants (action types, row-scoped triggers, durations, trigger eligibility) are held by 'Keep in sync' comments, and products.workflows has no tach interface block.
The 12 session turns are mostly workflows-as-code planning; one turn that was mostly a pasted teammate Slack message was not quoted, and only the read-only code-managed rule came from sessions.

Scope: `products/workflows` plus `nodejs/src/cdp/services/hogflows`, the workflow runtime. CODEOWNERS gives team-workflows all of `nodejs/src/cdp`; the rest of CDP (destinations, hog functions) was left out to keep the draft about workflows.

Sessions: T3 threads that run Claude also write the Claude Code store, so the same turn shows up twice and is counted once. Codex sessions started by an orchestrator (subagents) were skipped; only sessions Michael started count.
Jev on the AI gateway allowed 5 requests a minute, so it only classified session turns (5 per call). Review comments went to the Opus clustering pass unfiltered.
Two caveats that describe possible security gaps were left out of this public draft and handed to the team directly.

Shape: the #project-coherence discussion (Danilo, @daniloc, and Marce Coll) argued for a project glossary and theory-first development, with a THEORY.md of vocabulary, abstractions, invariants, boundaries, and non-goals, and for component roles that carry guarantees. The ladder is Coherence's: convention, totality-checked, enshrined.
